exceptions.reason: braces 3.0.3 is the latest release and the advisory, published 2026-09-18, covers <=3.0.3 with no patched version, so there is no upgrade to take and no override that resolves it. It cannot be designed out either: it arrives through micromatch 4.0.8, which the latest fast-glob (3.3.3), stylelint (17.16.0) and http-proxy-middleware (4.2.0) all still require, so @wordpress/scripts 36 would install it too. Unlike extract-zip this code does run: stylelint and fast-glob execute it during `npm run lint:css` and `npm run build`, on developer machines and in CI. It is classed build-test-transitive rather than ci because of where its input comes from, the same reasoning spec 056 applied to the minimatch and brace-expansion findings. The defect needs a deeply nested brace pattern, and the only glob patterns in play here are the built-in defaults of @wordpress/scripts: every invocation in this repository is a bare `wp-scripts` command with directory flags, no tracked file imports braces, micromatch, fast-glob or globby, and there is no custom webpack, stylelint or dev-server proxy configuration that could carry a pattern in. The lockfile does not mark braces dev-only, and that is an install edge rather than an import: @wordpress/theme, installed beneath @wordpress/components for corex-config, lists stylelint as an optional peer for a lint plugin it ships. @wordpress/components itself is externalised to the `wp-components` script handle, and no built asset contains braces, micromatch or stylelint code (checked against every workspace build/ directory on 2026-10-04).
exceptions.control: A successful trigger is an uncaught RangeError that ends one lint or build process: a failed job, with nothing read and nothing written (CVSS C:N/I:N/A:H). Supplying the pattern means committing a change to this repository's tooling configuration, which already grants arbitrary code execution in that same job, so the advisory adds nothing to what such an author could do. CI runs with `contents: read` and no production secrets. Nothing reaches a WordPress site: scripts/build-shared-host-dist.mjs ships plugin and theme source and excludes node_modules.
exceptions.upstreamTrigger: Remove when braces publishes a release above 3.0.3 that the advisory does not cover; micromatch requires ^3.0.3, so a lockfile update takes it with no override. Also removable if fast-glob, stylelint and http-proxy-middleware all stop depending on micromatch. This exception must be re-argued rather than renewed if a custom webpack or stylelint configuration, a dev-server proxy, or any script that passes an external value as a glob is added: the "patterns come only from tool defaults" half of the reasoning would no longer hold.

exceptions.reason: Published 2026-10-05: the unsafe-operation guard does not block git trailer command configuration. simple-git 3.36.0 is installed and the fix is in the 4.x line only. It is installed only beneath @wordpress/env (a devDependency), which uses it in two places: lib/download-sources.js, to clone and update the git sources named in a wp-env configuration, and lib/runtime/docker/download-wp-phpunit.js, to clone the WordPress test suite from a GitHub address written in that file. @wordpress/env 11.16.0, the latest release, requires simple-git ^3.32.3 and calls the package as a function (`require( 'simple-git' )( … )`). simple-git 4, where the fixes are, exports an object with a named `simpleGit` instead, so overriding it does not install a fix, it breaks `wp-env start`: the override was tried on 2026-10-07 and wp-env's own call sequence failed at the first line with "SimpleGit is not a function".
exceptions.control: The defect is a way round simple-git's refusal of dangerous git options, so it matters where somebody else chooses the arguments, the configuration or the environment simple-git is given. Here they come from one place: wp-env.json in this repository, which names a single git source, `WordPress/WordPress#master`, and the fixed option objects in wp-env's source. A person who can change that file can already run any command on the same machine through wp-env's documented `lifecycleScripts`, so the advisory gives them nothing they lack. It runs only when a developer starts wp-env (`npm run env:start`); no workflow under .github/ uses wp-env, and scripts/build-shared-host-dist.mjs ships plugin and theme source and never node_modules, so it reaches neither CI nor a WordPress site.
exceptions.upstreamTrigger: Remove when @wordpress/env publishes a release that depends on simple-git 4.0.1 or later; a lockfile update then takes it with no override. Re-argue instead of renewing if wp-env.json gains a source whose URL or ref is not written in this repository, or if a CI workflow starts using wp-env: either would end the reasoning above.

exceptions.reason: Published 2026-09-24 against sprintf-js <=1.1.3, and 1.1.3 is the latest release, so there is no upgrade to take. sprintf-js 1.0.3 is installed for argparse 1.0.10, which js-yaml 3.15.2 lists as a dependency. Two packages here use js-yaml 3: @wordpress/env, which calls `yaml.dump`, and @istanbuljs/load-nyc-config beneath Jest. Both use it as a library, and js-yaml's library code does not load argparse: the only file in js-yaml that requires it is bin/js-yaml.js, the command-line entry point, which no script, workflow or file in this repository invokes. So sprintf-js is installed and its code is not reached. Moving js-yaml to 4.x, which uses argparse 2 and no sprintf-js, was not done: it is a major version under two consumers that declare ^3, for a finding nothing here can trigger.
exceptions.control: The defect is a denial of service from an attacker-chosen precision in a format string. The only format strings on this path are argparse's own help and usage templates, printed when somebody runs the js-yaml command by hand. devDependency only: scripts/build-shared-host-dist.mjs ships plugin and theme source and never node_modules, so it reaches no WordPress site.
exceptions.upstreamTrigger: Remove when sprintf-js publishes a release above 1.1.3 that the advisory does not cover and argparse 1 accepts it (it requires ~1.0.2, so that needs an override), or when both @wordpress/env and @istanbuljs/load-nyc-config depend on js-yaml 4 or later, which carries no sprintf-js. Re-argue if any script here starts calling the js-yaml command.
